name: What happens if my basement concrete slab has moisture problems?

mainEntity.name: What happens if my basement concrete slab has moisture problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your basement experiences occasional water seepage or sits over damp ground, you must resolve active leaks and apply a dedicated waterproofing or uncoupling membrane before laying tile. While porcelain tile itself is waterproof, water trapped beneath tiles can break down standard adhesive bonds or push efflorescence salts up through the grout lines. Applying a liquid waterproofing membrane or sheet barrier over the cured concrete seals out moisture, protecting your tile installation from below-grade dampness.
acceptedAnswer.description: Moisture must be sealed with waterproofing or uncoupling membranes before tiling to prevent thin-set failure, loose tiles, and white mineral stains in grout.
